summary: Tafamidis (VYNDAQEL and VYNDAMAX) is an oral transthyretin (TTR) stabilizer indicated for the treatment of cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalization. Transthyretin is a transport protein that circulates as a tetramer; its dissociation into monomers allows misfolding and aggregation into amyloid fibrils that deposit in the myocardium. Tafamidis binds the TTR tetramer at the thyroxine-binding sites, kinetically stabilizing it and slowing amyloid formation. Vyndamax 61 mg and Vyndaqel 80 mg (four 20 mg capsules) deliver bioequivalent exposure and are not interchangeable on a per-milligram basis. The drug is generally well tolerated with few contraindications; the main label warning is potential fetal harm.

moa: Tafamidis is a selective stabilizer of transthyretin (TTR). TTR is a transport protein, normally a homotetramer, that carries thyroxine and retinol-binding protein. Tetramer dissociation into monomers is the rate-limiting step in the process by which TTR misfolds and aggregates into amyloid fibrils that deposit in tissues, including the myocardium, causing transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Tafamidis binds with high affinity and selectivity to the two thyroxine-binding sites of the native tetramer, kinetically stabilizing the tetramer and slowing its dissociation into monomers, thereby inhibiting amyloidogenesis.

preg: Based on findings from animal studies, tafamidis may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. In animal reproduction studies, oral administration during organogenesis produced fetal malformations, reduced fetal body weight, embryofetal death, and impaired offspring survival and growth at exposures relevant to humans. There are no adequate data in pregnant women; advise women of reproductive potential of the potential risk to a fetus.
lact: There are no data on the presence of tafamidis in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production. Tafamidis is present in the milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with tafamidis.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in patients with renal impairment. There are limited data in patients with severe renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate below 25 mL/min/1.73 m2).
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment. There are limited data in patients with severe hepatic impairment; exposure may differ, so use with awareness of the limited data.

major: No major drug interactions established; tafamidis has not shown clinically meaningful interactions in studies
moderate: Tafamidis may inhibit the efflux transporter BCRP; co-administration with BCRP substrates (e.g., methotrexate, rosuvastatin, imatinib) could increase their exposure - monitor for substrate-related toxicity
minor: Tafamidis may inhibit uptake transporters OAT1 and OAT3; clinical significance is low at recommended doses
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not require dosing changes.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction between tafamidis and alcohol has been described in the labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory test interference; no routine drug-specific laboratory monitoring is mandated by the label.

common: Adverse reactions occurred at frequencies similar to placebo in the pivotal trial; no adverse reaction was attributed specifically to tafamidis above placebo
serious: Serious adverse reactions specific to tafamidis were not identified; serious events generally reflected the underlying cardiomyopathy
emergency: Signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, swelling, difficulty breathing) - seek immediate care

missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: There is limited clinical experience with tafamidis overdose. The highest doses studied in healthy volunteers were well above the therapeutic dose without dose-limiting toxicity. In the event of overdose, institute general supportive measures and treat symptomatically as needed.
